attributes.proposal_description:
Blockchain interoperability is essential for the growth and adoption of decentralized technologies. As a leading blockchain network, Cardano has established itself as a secure, scalable, and research-driven ecosystem. However, interoperability with other blockchains remains limited. Wanchain’s XPort protocol offers a decentralized, secure, and efficient cross-chain data transfer solution, making it an ideal candidate to bridge Cardano with external blockchain ecosystems. This proposal is for the deployment of XPort to Cardano, enabling seamless cross-chain data transfers between Cardano and other blockchain networks.

About Cross-Chain Data Transfer Protocols

Cross-Chain Data Transfer Protocols enable data to be passed from one blockchain to another. Rather than only moving fungible and non-fungible tokens, which are a specific type of data structure, Cross-Chain Data Transfer Protocols can move any type of data. Importantly, Cross-Chain Data Transfer Protocols can feed data into 3rd party smart contracts to seamlessly execute on-chain logic and create novel cross-chain applications.

The basic flow of all Cross-Chain Data Transfers Protocols is as follows:

- A user or smart contract records arbitrary data on the source chain
- The off-chain component detects these data
- The off-chain component records these data on the destination chain
- A smart contract executes on-chain logic on the destination chain using these data

About XPort

True to its legacy, XPort is deceptively simple. It essentially just detects data on a source blockchain then exports it to the destination chain in the correct format.

XPort is composed of two basic elements: one robust off-chain relayer and a set of rudimentary on-chain smart contracts called Cross-Chain Gateways.

1. The off-chain relayer is the same Bridge Node Group that secures all cross-chain transactions executed using the Wanchain Bridge. These permissionless Bridge Nodes are rotated and re-elected monthly. They use Multiparty Computation and Shamir’s Secret Sharing cryptography to transfer messages and arbitrary data across chains.

2. A smart contract, called a Cross-Chain Gateway, is deployed on each supported blockchain. These Cross-Chain Gateways have limited functionality — they can essentially only send and receive data. They serve as the point of contact for all 3rd party developers.

Importantly, XPort is designed to be compliant with the Enterprise Ethereum Alliance’s Distributed Ledger Technology Interoperability Specification, co-authored by Wanchain’s VP on Engineering Dr. Weijia Zhang.

More technical information about XPort: https://docs.wanchain.org/latest-major-updates/xport-wanchains-cross-chain-data-transfer-protocol-development-handbook

attributes.problem_statement:
Seamless cross-chain communication is a challenge for permissionless blockchains due to their inherent lack of interoperability. This limitation is rooted in their trustless nature, as blockchains need a mechanism to verify the authenticity of data before processing it. When dealing with heterogeneous blockchain networks, each with their own distinct ruleset and security guarantees, cross-chain communication is currently impossible without the intervention of an off-chain component.

In many ways, this problem is just the oracle problem. The oracle problem, for those who are unfamiliar, refers to a blockchain’s inability to access external data, rendering it isolated. An additional piece of infrastructure — whether you want to call it a bridge, an oracle or a relayer — is needed to connect the blockchain and the off-chain data. With cross-chain communication, the problem is the same. The data that needs to be accessed just happens to be on another blockchain!

Cross-Chain Data Transfer Protocols enable data to be passed from one blockchain to another. Rather than only moving fungible and non-fungible tokens, which are a specific type of data structure, Cross-Chain Data Transfer Protocols can move any type of data. Importantly, Cross-Chain Data Transfer Protocols can feed data into 3rd party smart contracts to seamlessly execute on-chain logic and create novel cross-chain applications.

This proposal is to deploy XPort, Wanchain's cross-chain data transfer protocol, to Cardano.
attributes.proposal_benefit:
Once deployed, XPort will allow arbitrary data to flow between Cardano, any EVM, and select non-EVM networks. This will enable developers to develop applications that span multiple blockchains. It will also empower developers to shift their focus from extracting value out of a blockchain to importing execution logic into one. 

Other potential benefits include but are not limited to:

- Improved interoperability between Cardano and the of the industry
- Expanded access to liquidity and assets on other chains
- Greater abstraction to improve UX
- Reduced bridge risk
- Improved developer experience
- More modular application design/New types of applications
attributes.supplementary_endorsement: Wanchain is the longest running cross-chain bridge in the blockchain industry and is the primary cross-chain value bridge currently servicing the Cardano mainnet. It has received good support from the Cardano community (multiple approved Catalyst proposals) and Cardano Dapps (like Liqwid).

Hi there! Below are answers to your questions. Please let us know if you have any other follow-up questions!

Q1. What are the concrete Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) after deploying XPort to Cardano?

A: This is an interesting question, as XPort is ultimately a dev tool. As such, measuring the success via KPI is a little different than when dealing with a consumer app. For XPort, we measure # of supported networks, # of deployed routes, # of messages and error rate.

That being said, the presence of this kind of tool (broadly, the category would be “Cross-chain message passing protocols” or “Cross-chain data transfer protocols”), will benefit the Cardano ecosystem by:

- Improving interoperability between Cardano and the rest of the industry
- Expanding access to liquidity and assets on other chains
- Improving UX via abstraction
- Reducing bridge risk
- Improving developer experience
- Enabling more modular application design and, therefore, new types of applications

Q2. How will the KPIs be measured, at what intervals, and by what method of validation?The proposal mentions that developers will be able to use XPort.

A: XPort is open to developers. We track # of supported networks, # of deployed routes and # of messages in real time. We track error rates on a monthly interval.

Q3. How many developers or projects are expected to actually adopt it?

A: Difficult to accurately estimate, but we have already received requests from ~10 Cardano projects that can’t be serviced without a protocol like XPort.

Q4. How will claims like “improved developer experience” or “better UX” be quantified and validated?

A: It won’t be quantified. It is moreso a qualitative statement based on developers approaching us with an idea that can’t be serviced properly by Wanchain’s existing Cardano bridge.

5. Has this proposal been sufficiently socialized on platforms like X (formerly Twitter) and other social media, and does it have broad support within the Cardano community? What evidence can you provide?

A: The proposal has been shared and discussed on an X Space in the Deep forum: https://x.com/cryptstitution/status/1909494347281973600

Hi there! Thank you for your questions. Our answers are below. Please let us know if you have any other questions!

Q1: How XPort can leverage Cardano's technical advantages

A: Cardano’s infrastructure will give great confidence in the security of the XPort components that are deployed on Cardano. However, when dealing with interoperability, you need to consider the risk profile of every single connected chain. The ultimate goal of XPort isn’t only about leveraging Cardano’s unique technical advantages, but to serve as a kind of “translation” layer to allow applications to seamlessly work between multiple chains including Cardano. In other words, it’s to make it possible for developers to deploy parts of their applications on Cardano while keeping other parts of their applications on other chains. This allows applications to benefit from the unique advantages of each chain.

Q2: About KPI measurements when implementing XPort on Cardano

A: For XPort, we measure # of supported networks, # of deployed routes, # of messages and error rate.

Let me start with the projects this could help.

For me, the lowest hanging fruit are the DEXs on Cardano (e.g., Minswap, Wingriders, VyFi, SundaeSwap, Muesliswap, etc). Having access to a data transfer protocol/message passing protocol will make it relatively straightforward for them to add "cross-chain swap" functionality to their applications (without sacrificing decentralisation). 

Following that, XPort will also make it a more reasonable ask for EVM-based DEXs to support Cardano in addition to their existing chains (the biggest EVM dexs probably won't be interested, but small/mid-sized DEXs may be intrigued by the high-growth potential of Cardano).

Another powerful user case is that XPort will allow the creation of so-called Omnichain tokens on Cardano. These are tokens that are natively bridgeable -- meaning they get burned/minted on all supported chains, rather than being locked in a 3rd party bridge. In recent years, this type of token has been popularised by LayerZero on EVM chains. There's no shortage of projects who could take advantage of this.

Finally, more complex scenarios are possible as well (e,g., cross-chain lending for Liqwid/Fluid Tokens), though the specific implementation will depend on the specific user case.
Thank you for your feedback! Happy to hear that the North American Community Hub saw XPort's potential to improve Cardano interoperability.

We contacted Wanchain about their solutions to support cross-chain dapp functionality for Cardano native applications and found that the lack of this xport (or similar trusted technology by which Cardano smart contracts can effectively interact with data from other blockchain assets) was a blocker. From our discussions with Wanchain, we understand their proposal here to be fully open sourced and that fees associated with the tool will be minimized to cover gas fees, which we feel qualifies this proposal as something that we would also support as Cardano community members. 

If there is another proposal or already in-progress development initiative to solve this cross-chain oracle problem, we would like to be made aware of it, because in this case it isn't the best use of treasury resources to duplicate efforts, but we are encouraged by the fact that Wanchain is one of the largest / most trusted bridges in crypto with successful crosschain oracle use cases across a number of other blockchains already, which lead us to trust this oracle solution and we believe could lead other developers to trust it as well, ultimately unlocking crosschain dapp interoperability between Cardano and other blockchains.

Our dapp (l4va.com in development) is an open source decentralized asset fractionalization platform, allowing users to mint new fungible tokens representing governance over assets locked in smart contracts and we would love to make our application cross-chain with a tool like xport, so that we can wrap assets from ETH / other chains that have larger adoption and traction, creating a unique value offering for investors in CNTs minted that represent diverse baskets of RWAs and other assets. 

Until this cross-chain oracle is built, or something similar, we will be unable to realize our cross-chain goal. 

We generally support this proposal from the perspective of supporting the Cardano treasury investing in achieving cross-chain oracle functionality, and from our diligence we have found that Wanchain have a trusted track record of building this type of infrastructure, so if they build it we will most likely use it.

Conecptually I agree with the the utility of projects like XPort. Bridges are often only for assets, whereas often time bridging data is more powerful and more flexible and I've often run into this need when building applicatitons myself. At the same time, I think there are some subtle tricks on how to handle this given Cardano's UTXO model that I would like to see more fleshed out in this proposal.

I think if you resubmitted this proposal in the future with a more concrete architecture plan with an app that plans to leverage this, it would be easier to support this. Otherwise, given the number of treasury budget proposals, it's a bit hard to prioritize this for the first budget

Just as an additional piece of information, deploying XPort will enable Wanchain to add Cardano support to XFlows, our canonical cross-chain swap. So that could be considered the "first" app that will leverage XPort, so to speak. Regardless, thank you for the thoughtful feedback!
